title: The unextended semisimple Gelfand--Kirillov conjecture
statement: For a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, is its enveloping quotient division ring a Weyl division ring over a purely transcendental central field? The P929 formulation also gestures toward the wider algebraic-Lie-algebra setting.
status: As of November 2026, The general statement is false; type A is established, and the reviewed literature still leaves simple types \(C_n\), \(n\ge2\), and \(G_2\) unresolved. Reuse the existing problem identity GP-1967-21; this row supplies the additional occurrence, not a replacement of earlier occurrences. A finite central extension changes the question.

title: Projective structures on the real line
statement: Classify connected real projective one-manifolds diffeomorphic to \(\mathbb R\), up to projective diffeomorphism.
status: As of November 2026, Resolved: the full universal projective line, a half-line, and the positive half-integral winding classes of bounded intervals; see \citet[Corollary 4.16]{belgunmoroianu2025projective}, which attributes the open-curve result to Kuiper (1954).

title: Levi-flat filling of real two-spheres
statement: For a specified smooth embedded sphere \(S\subset\mathbb C^2\), determine whether it bounds a Levi-flat hypersurface foliated by analytic discs.
status: As of November 2026, The two-elliptic-point sphere in a strictly pseudoconvex boundary is fillable by Bedford--Gaveau (1983); arbitrary spheres are not universally fillable. \citet[Theorem 1.1 and Introduction]{gaussiersukhov2011filling} supplies a precise later extension and records the counterexamples. This entry does not assert an exhaustive classification of all embeddings.

title: Categorical characterization of D-affinity
statement: For a smooth separated finite-type complex variety, does equivalence of the natural global-sections/localization adjunction for quasi-coherent left D-modules imply vanishing of all higher sheaf cohomology and generation by global sections?
status: As of November 2026, Yes. Beilinson’s 10 November continuation, 1980-498.2--3, gives the projective-generator and \v{C}ech argument. This is a resolved question, not a present open problem.

title: Infinite-dimensional algebras with a multiplicative norm
statement: Does a real infinite-dimensional normed vector space admit a continuous bilinear multiplication satisfying \(\|xy\|=\|x\|\|y\|\)? Does the answer change when a two-sided identity is required?
status: As of November 2026, Yes without a unit, by the Hilbert tensor-coordinate construction; no with a unit, by Urbanik--Wright (1960). The notebook does not choose the unit convention, so this is a resolved disambiguation rather than a currently open problem.

title: Continuity and differentiability of Thomae functions
statement: For \(T_\alpha(p/q)=q^{-\alpha}\) in lowest terms and \(T_\alpha(x)=0\) for irrational \(x\), determine continuity and differentiability, including \(\alpha=1\).
status: As of November 2026, this is a solved classical exercise. For \(\alpha>0\), continuity holds exactly at irrational points; for \(\alpha\leq0\) there are no continuity points. For \(0<\alpha\leq2\) there are no differentiability points. For \(\alpha>2\), at an irrational point with convergent denominators \(q_k\), differentiability is equivalent to \(q_{k+1}/q_k^{\alpha-1}\to0\), and the derivative is zero. The criterion is supplied by the elementary convergent estimate in the companion; \citet{varona2009differentiability} documents the classical general-power problem and its earlier literature.

title: A single continuous-function limit for the Dirichlet function
statement: Can the indicator of the rational numbers on \(\mathbb R\), already expressed by an iterated pointwise limit in the notes, be the pointwise limit of one sequence of continuous real-valued functions?
status: As of November 2026, the answer is no: Baire-one real functions on \(\mathbb R\) have a dense set of continuity points, whereas this indicator is nowhere continuous. This is an application of the classical Baire criterion, read in \citet[p.173]{baire1900nouvelle}.

title: Large-frequency asymptotics of Gaussian, quartic, and sextic Fourier integrals
statement: Determine the asymptotics as \(\lambda\to+\infty\) of \(\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-x^p}\cos(\lambda x)\,dx\) for \(p=2,4,6\).
status: As of November 2026, this is a solved steepest-descent exercise. The Gaussian is \(\sqrt\pi e^{-\lambda^2/4}\); the higher powers have exponentially damped oscillatory leading terms from a conjugate pair of dominant saddles, explicitly reconstructed in the occurrence. The method and branch convention are checked against \citet[\S2.4(iv)]{nist2026dlmf}. No new asymptotic theorem is claimed.

title: Isomorphic cohomology without a direct chain map
statement: Find complexes with isomorphic cohomology for which a prescribed cohomology isomorphism cannot be induced by a chain map in the stated direction.
status: As of November 2026, this is a solved exercise: \(A=(\mathbb Z/2)[0]\) and \(B=[\mathbb Z\xrightarrow{2}\mathbb Z]\) in degrees \(-1,0\) have the same cohomology, but every map \(A\to B\) is zero. Their derived-category isomorphism is represented by the reverse quasi-isomorphism, inverted by localization. Earlier occurrence 1971-266.3 concerns the general derived-category universal property, not the exact counterexample question, so its problem identifier is not reused.

title: Genus from a Newton polygon
statement: Determine the genus of the smooth projective model of a generic irreducible plane Laurent curve with prescribed two-dimensional Newton polygon.
status: As of November 2026, the problem is solved under Newton nondegeneracy: the genus is the number of interior lattice points. Khovanskii's 1978 publication predates this exposition; the question is a motivating problem, not an open 1981 conjecture.

title: Root counts from prescribed Newton polytopes
statement: For a generic square system of Laurent polynomials with prescribed Newton polytopes, determine the number of roots in the algebraic torus, with multiplicity.
status: As of November 2026, Bernshtein's 1975 theorem gives \(n!\) times ordinary mixed volume, with equality under the appropriate initial-system nondegeneracy. The notebook presents a problem already solved before this lecture. Earlier local Newton-polyhedron questions are related but not exact recurrences.

title: Newton-type asymptotic root count for complex exponential sums
statement: Extend the Laurent-polynomial root count to the density of roots of a regular square system of finite exponential sums with complex spectra.
status: As of November 2026, this formulation is solved by Kazarnovskii's 1981 regular-system theorem, with leading coefficient \(\kappa_n n!P_n/(2\pi)^n\) and remainder \(O(R^{n-1})\). The theorem requires its face-system regularity; arbitrary fixed systems are outside the assertion.

title: Relating exponential zero density to the growth indicatrix
statement: Explain how the exponential-sum zero-density theorem is expressed through the support functions of the spectral convex bodies, as asked by I. M. Gelfand on 2 March 1981.
status: As of November 2026, the finite-spectrum connection is established through the mixed Monge--Ampère integral already in \citet[\S1(c)]{kazarnovskii1981zeros}. \citet{kazarnovskii2024distribution} extends this framework to averaged zero currents of regular finite-dimensional spaces of entire functions of exponential growth. The later result is not a universal fixed-system convergence theorem, and the notebook does not specify such a conjecture.

title: Genus-two spectral curves of rational commuting differential operators
statement: For a smooth projective genus-two curve over \(\mathbb C\), choose a hyperelliptic model \(w^2=z^5+\beta_4z^4+\cdots+\beta_0\). There exist commuting rational-coefficient ordinary differential operators \(L,M\) whose spectral curve is this model and whose generic common eigenspace has dimension two. The coordinate map is faithful. If instead one insists on every given affine equation \(P\), including a presentation with a nonconstant unit, the analogous ordinary-operator assertion is false; the notebook does not distinguish these readings.
status: As of November 2026, every smooth projective complex genus-two curve, and every standard monic quintic hyperelliptic model, is realized by rational commuting operators. This is an established result. Universal realization of every affine presentation is false, as the chapter demonstrates using \(zw^2-z^4-1=0\); this distinction is not promoted to an artificial residual open problem.

title: Curve function fields in the first Weyl division ring
statement: For every smooth projective integral curve \(C/\mathbb C\), does there exist a unital \(\mathbb C\)-embedding \(\mathbb C(C)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(A_1(\mathbb C))\), where \(A_1=\mathbb C\langle x,D\rangle/(Dx-xD-1)\)? Singular integral curves give the same question after normalization.
status: As of November 2026, all complex curves of genus at most two and explicit higher-genus families have positive realizations. No source proving or disproving the universal curve-function-field conjecture was located in the documented search. This is a search limitation, not a claim that no such theorem exists.

title: Spectra of sums of Hermitian matrices and tensor-product multiplicities
statement: For real weakly decreasing \(n\)-tuples \(x,y,z\), characterize the existence of complex Hermitian \(n\times n\) matrices \(X,Y\) whose eigenvalue lists are \(x,y\) and whose sum has eigenvalue list \(z\). Trace equality is necessary and is retained in the final characterization.
status: As of November 2026, the Horn problem is solved by the recursive inequalities, equivalently by the honeycomb and representation-theoretic criteria.
